text:
Alex (Support): Hey team, DataPipeOps is seeing intermittent 429s after they migrated a heavy nightly embed job to eu-dedicated-3 yesterday. They say it used to be stable and now some batches get throttled mid-run. Can we triage?

DataPipeOps (customer): FYI: our job runs ~120 parallel workers, each calling /v1/generate for embeddings. Since the move we started seeing ~10-15% of requests return 429s with no obvious pattern. Logs show x-rate-limit-remaining sometimes at 0 and then back up. Cost also spiked because of retries.

Alex (Support): Can you paste a sample 429 response (headers + body) and approximate wall time this started? Any config changes on your side?

DataPipeOps (customer): No config change on our side other than pointing to the new endpoint. Sample response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 400
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 12
content-type: application/json
{ "error": { "message": "rate limit exceeded: reserved_pool quota exhausted (eu-dedicated-3)", "code": 429 }}
```
This started around 22:15 UTC last night and persisted in small spikes until 23:05.

Priya (SRE): Thanks. Two quick things: 1) Did the customer burst beyond their per-account share within the reserved pool? 2) Any recent deployment/changes on eu-dedicated-3?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: eu-dedicated-3 config refresh at 2025-11-03T21:58:04Z (rev: cfg-20251103-18)

Tom (Eng-runtime): Noted. The config refresh was a small routing + slot rebalancing; shouldn't change per-account caps but could affect transient KV cache warmup. Alex, can you ask for the header x-rwd-reserved-pool-usage if present? That helps map pool-level exhaustion.

DataPipeOps (customer): Header snippet when 429 occurred: 
```
x-reserved-pool: eu-dedicated-3
x-reserved-pool-cap: 200
x-reserved-pool-used: 198
x-account-share-cap: 50
x-account-share-used: 50
```

Priya (SRE): Ok that is the smoking gun — pool capacity nearly saturated and their account share hit the per-account cap, so they hit 429s while the pool had only a couple free slots. Sounds like their job concurrency is higher than the per-account concurrency limit.

Alex (Support): They claim this job used to run fine before moving to eu-dedicated-3. Could be that previous pool had different per-account share or transient lower utilization. We need repro steps to confirm. Can we get a lightweight reproduction so Eng-runtime can test?

Tom (Eng-runtime): Please have them run this minimal repro (single-machine concurrency) so we can reproduce locally: 
```
# GNU parallel + curl example
seq 1 120 | parallel -j120 \
  "curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{elapsed_total}s\n' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
   -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
   -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
   -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-embed-1\",\"input\":\"test\"}'"
```
If that yields 429s quickly, capture headers. Also set concurrency down to 50 to see behavior.

DataPipeOps (customer): Running now, will report.

Jordan (Acct): Quick note on billing: their retry storm pushed token counts up ~30% during the window. We may want to consider pro-rating or a one-off credit if this was caused by capacity misalignment on our side — pending root cause.

Priya (SRE): While they repro, Tom — can you check pool allocation and per-account caps for eu-dedicated-3? Config lives in infra: 
```
reserved_pools:
  - name: eu-dedicated-3
    capacity_total_qps: 400
    account_max_qps: 50
    burst_window_secs: 10
    backfill_share: 0.2
```
If account_max_qps=50 then 120 concurrent workers would easily trip the per-account limit assuming each worker makes ~1r/s.

Tom (Eng-runtime): Confirmed current pool config matches that YAML. There's also a soft-burst policy but it requires free pool headroom. If pool is near-saturated, soft-burst won't help. I can temporarily bump this customer's account_max_qps from 50 -> 80 as a mitigation (no code deploy, just a config flag change) — would you like me to do that?

Alex (Support): Customer approval required for temporary change? Jordan, is this covered under existing enterprise tailored configs?

Jordan (Acct): DataPipeOps is on a Dedicated reserved package with some flex. I'll authorize a one-off per-account increase for tonight while we investigate. Alex, please tell them to pause large retries and we'll flip the flag.

DataPipeOps (customer): Thanks. We'll pause retries and re-run the job after you flip. How long will the temporary increase last?

Tom (Eng-runtime): I can set a TTL on the override for 2 hours to limit exposure. Making change now.

deploy-bot: config-change: override applied to account datapipeops — account_max_qps set to 80 (ttl: 2h) by tom; change id cfg-override-9831

DataPipeOps (customer): Re-ran the job. So far 0 429s in first 25 minutes. Big improvement. Thanks. :white_check_mark:

Priya (SRE): Good. Action items: 1) Tom to analyze pool utilization patterns to see why eu-dedicated-3 has high occupancy compared to other pools (maybe noisy neighbors or balancing). 2) Alex/Jordan coordinate with customer to schedule a permanent increase or capacity move. 3) Support to recommend client-side backoff/retry jitter to avoid billing spikes.

Tom (Eng-runtime): On it — I'll pull per-slot utilization and recent placement decisions for the last 48h and follow up in this thread with a short summary and recommended long-term fixes (increase pool capacity or move some heavy accounts to a different reserved pool).

Alex (Support): Also recommending customer implement exponential backoff + capped retries. Sample snippet we gave them: 
```
# python requests simple backoff
for attempt in range(5):
    r = requests.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
    if r.status_code == 200:
        break
    if r.status_code == 429:
        sleep((2 ** attempt) + random.random())
```

Jordan (Acct): I'll open a billing ticket to review the retry-related overage and propose a goodwill credit depending on root cause.

DataPipeOps (customer): Appreciate the quick help. Please ping when you have the pool analysis.

Priya (SRE): Marking this triage resolved for now. We'll leave the thread open for the follow-up analysis. :mag:
